punchline: In Goleman's data the average performers overrate themselves and the stars often underrate themselves.
thirty_sec: Daniel Goleman cites studies where accurate self-assessment marked star performers, among several hundred knowledge workers at firms like AT&T and 3M. On 360-degree ratings, average performers overestimated their strengths, while stars rarely did and sometimes underestimated theirs, which he links to high internal standards. A gap in this skill, he says, can derail a career. The fix he points toward is time to look at yourself honestly.
